title: Best 8 CDC Tools for Cloud Data Warehouse in 2026
summary: Compare the best CDC tools for cloud data warehouses in 2026: Artie, Debezium, Fivetran, Airbyte, AWS DMS, and more on latency, sources, and pricing.
body_markdown:
### Are CDC tools only used for cloud data warehouses?


No. The same capture mechanism powers event-driven architectures, cache invalidation, cross-database replication, search index updates, and real-time application features. Cloud data warehouses are the most common destination because that is where analytics and dashboards read from, and it is the destination this guide evaluates against.


### What is the best CDC tool for a cloud data warehouse?


There is no single best CDC tool for every team. Debezium is the best open-source option if you want to own the whole pipeline. Artie is the best managed option for low-latency CDC into cloud warehouses. Fivetran is the best fit if connector breadth matters more than latency, and AWS DMS or Google Datastream are the best choices when you are fully committed to one cloud and its native warehouse.


### What is the difference between CDC tools and ETL tools?


ETL and ELT tools extract data on a schedule, usually by querying source tables, and load it in batches. CDC tools read the database transaction log and stream individual row changes continuously. Many ELT platforms, including Fivetran and Airbyte, offer CDC connectors, but they still deliver on a sync schedule. Purpose-built CDC tools deliver each change within seconds of commit.


### What are the best open-source CDC tools?


Debezium is the most widely used open-source CDC engine and the one most other tools build on. Airbyte is an open-source ELT platform that embeds Debezium for its database CDC connectors. Both are free to run but require your team to operate Kafka or a sync scheduler, monitor replication lag, and handle schema changes in the warehouse.


### How do CDC tools affect the source database?


Log-based CDC tools read from the transaction log the database already writes, so the streaming path does not run heavy queries against production tables. The costs are a replication connection, logical decoding CPU, and retained log while the CDC client catches up. A stalled consumer can pin WAL on a Postgres primary until the disk fills, so monitor replication slot size. Initial backfills still read source tables, which is why tools that read from a replica and run backfills online matter.


### Can CDC tools handle schema changes?


It depends on the tool. Debezium emits schema change events but leaves the warehouse DDL to you. AWS DMS and Datastream handle a subset of changes and may require a reload for the rest. Managed platforms like Artie detect DDL changes and apply additive columns, type changes, and deletes to the destination automatically. Ask each vendor what happens for an added column, a dropped column, a type change, and a renamed table.
